intended_object: The duality isomorphism K₀(R) ≅ K₀(Rᵒᵖ) for an arbitrary ring R. It is induced by P ↦ P* = Hom_R(P, R), which sends finitely generated projective right R-modules to finitely generated projective right Rᵒᵖ-modules (Weibel, The K-book, Ch. II). I took this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
In this library, `K0 R` is `Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup (ProjectiveClass R)`, i.e. the localization at ⊤ (the group completion) of the monoid of isomorphism classes of finite projective right R-modules, with direct sum as addition.

`ProjectiveClass.dualEquiv R` is an additive equivalence of these class monoids. It sends [M] to the class of Hom_{Rᵐᵒᵖ}(M, R), which is a left R-module; restriction of scalars along Rᵐᵒᵖᵐᵒᵖ ≅ R turns it into a right Rᵐᵒᵖ-module, i.e. an Rᵐᵒᵖᵐᵒᵖ-module. This is the standard duality functor. The construction shows that it is additive, respects isomorphisms and is invertible, with the double dual identified via the bidual map.

`K0.dualEquiv` is the map this equivalence induces on the group completions, via `addEquivOfAddEquiv` for the localizations at ⊤. The side condition (the image of ⊤ is ⊤) holds by surjectivity. This is exactly the induced isomorphism K₀(R) ≅ K₀(Rᵒᵖ). The companion lemmas confirm the expected values: [M] ↦ [M*], the class of R maps to the class of Rᵒᵖ, and applying the duality twice gives the change of rings along R ≅ Rᵒᵖᵒᵖ.

The ring is arbitrary, with no commutativity assumed, so the generality is the natural one. Mathlib has no algebraic K₀ or K₀-duality to compare against.
